symptom: building pluggable widgets was 21 s of a 77 s settled re-run of 600 pages, 9.5 s of it in LoadWidgetTemplate: 2,104 template loads for 300 data grids and their filters (ako/mxcli#2160)
cause: GetTemplateFullBSON calls augmentFromMPK for every widget instance, and that deep-cloned the embedded template and merged the project's widget package into the clone every time. Finding the package and parsing it were already cached for the life of the process; the clone and the merge, which depend on nothing but those two cached values, were not
file: modelsdk/widgets/loader.go (augmentFromMPK, augmentedCache keyed by template and parsed package), modelsdk/widgets/augment_cache_test.go
insight: The obvious test - the kept template deep-equals a fresh augmentation - failed on the first widget, and not because of the cache: two fresh augmentations are not equal to each other, since AugmentTemplate mints an ID for each property it adds. That is harmless for sharing, because a load replaces every $ID again (collectIDs), but it means equality has to be stated modulo IDs, and the test first shows that two fresh augmentations agree in everything else before using that comparison for the kept one. Sharing is only sound while a load reads the template and changes nothing, so the kept template is compared again after four loads. Keying by the two pointers rather than by widget ID and path makes the cache exactly as fresh as the caches it reads from. The end-to-end check that settled it: the same 600-page script run on two copies with the old and the new binary gives 1,719 units whose canonical digests (IDs numbered by first appearance) are identical. Measured: settled re-run 83.1 s -> 73.9 s, first run of 600 pages 29.5 s -> 26.5 s, output and describe identical.
